## Philosophy quotes about learning

Learning is philosophy’s practical twin: how judgment is formed through study, error, dialogue, and habit.

14 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

### Why this theme matters

Education is not only information transfer; it is the shaping of attention and character. Confucian learning, Socratic midwifery, and Deweyan growth offer rival models.

### In the history of philosophy

Academies, monasteries, universities, and modern schooling all encode philosophies of learning—often silently.

[Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Confucius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/confucius) , [Zengzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zengzi) , [Xunzi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/xunzi) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Zhu Xi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/zhu-xi) , [Wang Guowei](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-guowei) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne)

### Frequently asked questions

#### What do philosophers say about learning?

They treat learning as cultivation of reason and character, not merely accumulation of facts.

#### Who emphasizes learning most?

Confucius, Plato, Dewey, and many Stoic teachers make education central to the good life.

#### Where are philosophy quotes about learning?
